detailed_rationale:
FACT is a Kerala-based, Government of India-controlled fertiliser manufacturer (DAP/NPK complex fertilisers under the FACTAMFOS brand, ammonium sulphate, caprolactam) whose realizations run substantially through the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme - the government sets per-nutrient subsidy rates administratively, FACT sells at MRP-plus-accrued-subsidy, and collects the subsidy leg with a lag. That mechanism is the story of FY26. Global input costs have spiked hard this year - sulphur prices have roughly doubled since January 2026 and DAP itself moved up another ~10% in April on tight global supply - while NBS rates don't reprice in real time. The squeeze shows up directly in FACT's numbers: Q3 FY26 (Oct-Dec 2025) revenue grew 65% YoY to Rs 1,567.84 crore, yet operating margin went to -2.73%, the worst in eight quarters, and the company posted a Rs 67.90 crore net loss against a Rs 20.86 crore profit the prior quarter and an Rs 8.00 crore profit a year earlier. That is a real, cash-relevant margin failure - revenue growing while the manufacturing spread goes negative - not an accounting illusion, and it is a sector-wide phenomenon: Chambal and other P&K names moved on the same 'FY27 fertiliser subsidy bill could double from the Budgeted Rs 1.7 trillion' headlines in June 2026, confirming this is an industry cost-price scissor, not FACT-specific execution failure.

On the interest-coverage flag specifically - I'd push back on treating it as pure subsidy-timing noise, and equally push back on treating it as a clean signal of company-specific distress. Two different things are bundled in that one ratio. First, total borrowings roughly doubled in FY26 (Rs 1,805 crore at Mar-2025 to Rs 3,985 crore at Mar-2026, debt-to-equity reaching 2.79x, its highest on record) - that increase has the fingerprints of a subsidy-receivable-funded working-capital gap, the textbook fertiliser-PSU pattern of drawing short-term debt against government dues not yet paid, and it is a lower-risk kind of leverage than it looks (the counterparty is sovereign, not a disputed private receivable). Second, and this is the part that shouldn't be waved away: in Q3 FY26 EBIT-to-interest coverage was actually negative (-0.69x) - operating losses, not merely thin coverage - and even stripping out Rs 39.21 crore of other income that cushioned the quarter, the underlying pre-tax loss would have been Rs 74.06 crore. That's a genuine operating-margin failure where input costs simply outran realizations that quarter, independent of financing timing. The subsequent two quarters look better - Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin came back to a positive (if still thin) level well below the prior year's 8%+, and Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026 quarter) printed Rs 1,042.77 crore of sales against only Rs 4.28 crore of net profit - so the trough is probably behind the company, but sub-1% net margins are not a coverage ratio that's been fixed, just one that's stopped bleeding. (A data-quality note on that Q4 read: the single source carrying an absolute Q4 FY26 profit figure reported it inconsistently, so I have deliberately leaned only on the directionally-reliable facts there - the EBITDA-margin recovery and the confirmed DAP-line start-up - and not on any one reported Q4 profit number.)

On growth and valuation: the deceleration the quant score is flagging is real and not merely a base-effect artifact - three consecutive quarters of sub-1% (or negative) net margins against a business with roughly flat five-year volume growth is not a compounder having a rough quarter, it's a subsidy-linked commodity processor whose profitability is currently a function of a government rate-reset lag. Against that operating reality, screener-level data flags FACT trading close to 40x book value on a three-year ROE of under 9% - a combination that is very hard to justify on fundamentals alone. The 2026 re-rating looks driven far more by sector narrative (the subsidy-bill-doubling chatter, and FACT's own May-2026 DAP line start-up at Udyogamandal) than by anything that has actually shown up in delivered profitability, which is precisely the setup - a stretched multiple sitting on top of a business that posted a negative-interest-coverage quarter within the last twelve months - that should worry a holder more than the headline order/subsidy story comforts them.
recommendation_rationale: Sell, affirmed rather than overridden. The research nuances the quant flag - part of the debt build and coverage weakness is a genuine, low-credit-risk subsidy-timing artifact common to NBS-linked fertiliser PSUs - but it does not reverse it: Q3 FY26's EBIT/interest ratio was actually negative, meaning operating profit alone (not just after financing cost) failed to cover costs that quarter, and growth over three years is negative in reality, not merely decelerating. With the stock priced near 40x book value and a reverse-DCF-implied growth rate nowhere close to what's been delivered, the valuation is underwriting a subsidy-driven recovery narrative that has only just begun to show up as thin (sub-1%) quarterly profits. That is a poor risk-reward for a name already held, even though near-term solvency risk is low given sovereign ownership and a sovereign subsidy receivable.
summary: FACT is a subsidy-administered fertiliser PSU whose FY26 P&L was hit by a real, sector-wide gap between spiking global input costs (sulphur roughly doubling year-to-date, DAP up further in April) and lagging NBS subsidy-rate resets - producing an actual negative EBIT-to-interest quarter in Q3 FY26 and a debt load that roughly doubled YoY to fund the resulting working-capital gap; Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 have stabilized back to thin, sub-1% profitability, so the worst is probably behind it, but the business is still barely self-funding on operating profit alone. Sitting on top of that is a stock trading near 40x book value on a sub-9% three-year ROE and a reverse-DCF gap that is among the widest in this sample - a valuation that reflects 2026's sector subsidy narrative and the new Udyogamandal DAP line rather than anything yet delivered in the numbers, and a 68th-percentile Quality score that looks like a stale, longer-lookback artifact from the FY22-24 global-fertiliser-price boom rather than a read on the current trajectory.
positive_para: The genuine bull case is narrower than the recent stock move implies, but it exists: FACT has actually started DAP production at Udyogamandal (from 15 May 2026, under NBS approval granted that April) - incremental, already-operating subsidised volume, not a slide-deck promise - and the subsidy receivable funding its debt build, once the timing gap closes, is a sovereign obligation with effectively no credit risk, unlike a disputed private-sector receivable. If the sector chatter that the FY27 fertiliser subsidy bill could double from its Rs 1.7 trillion budget estimate actually translates into faster or higher realizations for P&K players, that directly repairs FACT's margin and coverage math without needing any change in volumes, and the last two quarters (Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27) have already shown the operating-loss trough reversing into small positive profit - tentative evidence that the worst of the input-cost squeeze is behind rather than ahead.
negative_para: The bear case is that the market is paying well ahead of a recovery that has barely begun to show in the numbers: three straight quarters of sub-1% or negative net margins, an EBIT/interest ratio that was actually negative as recently as Q3 FY26, and total debt that roughly doubled in a year to bridge the gap - all while the stock trades near 40x book value pricing in growth nowhere close to the roughly -3% three-year revenue CAGR actually delivered. Because FACT's realizations are administratively set rather than market-set, there's no guarantee the next NBS reset is fast or large enough to fully offset another leg of sulphur/phosphoric-acid/ammonia inflation, so the same cost-price scissor that produced the Q3 FY26 loss can recur; a PSU fertiliser name priced for a growth story on the back of one new product line and a sector subsidy headline is one where a delayed rate reset, a renewed input spike, or simply a fade in the 2026 PSU re-rating theme leaves a long way to fall.
reverse_dcf_judgment: [OPINION] Something else, not a delivered recovery being priced in - 40x book on a sub-9% ROE is not a solvable reverse-DCF/residual-income output even under a best-case full-subsidy-reset-plus-DAP-ramp scenario (that arithmetic needs sustained ROE in the 30-40%+ zone, unsupported by anything here); this reads as sector-wide PSU re-rating/theme momentum (subsidy-bill-doubling headlines, the broader 2026 PSU re-rating wave) riding on the one real catalyst, not a market that has actually modeled and priced a subsidy-cycle recovery.

The negative-EBIT/interest Q3 FY26 finding is grounded in the cited Q3 net loss plus a transparent ex-other-income derivation and is stated at appropriate (not overclaimed) confidence, so I hold high conviction in the Sell.
